races.name: Adam Scott Celebratory Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Smoke Trail
runners_data.note: Front-runner with highest OR 118 but 51 days off and trainer form concerning at 2/32
runners_data.comment: Yet to progress from course win in October but still has a big role to play
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any significant further progress since making all in 14-runner course maiden (2m, good to soft) on rules debut in October but wasn't beaten far when fourth of six in Newbury handicap (2m, good to soft) in February and ought to play a significant role in this.

runners_data.name: Thorneylands
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader who showed clear promise in two Carlisle novice hurdles over similar distances
runners_data.comment: Close second in a bumper and also showed clear promise on both hurdling starts
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in Newcastle bumper (good to soft) in December and displayed clear promise in two Carlisle novice hurdles (both 2m1f, good to soft) this year, albeit he was pulled up on run-in after losing his action last time; others have more compelling claims here, though.

runners_data.name: Herja
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over 2m4f at Sedgefield, suited by strong gallop and good ground form
runners_data.comment: Safely held in two chases in March but consistent at a fair level over hurdles in 2025
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held in two chases last month but consistently showed a fair level of form over hurdles in 2025, gaining her win in Sedgefield maiden (2m4f, good) in September; big player back in this sphere; hood left off today.

runners_data.name: Nobotheratall
runners_data.note: Made all in Carlisle bumper but disappointed as 7th on hurdle debut behind two of today's rivals
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; ran well for a long way on hurdle debut and might come on for the outing
runners_data.spotlight: Delivered on earlier promise when making all in good-ground Carlisle bumper in October; behind two of today's rivals when weakening seventh on hurdle debut here (2m, good to soft) this month but ran well for a long way and wasn't beaten far; can feature if that outing brought him on.

runners_data.name: Bogha Baiste
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been placed twice at big odds recently including behind Changemyluck
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on hurdling debut but placed twice at big odds since; could have a say
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up on hurdle debut in January but placed twice at big odds since, more recently when 80-1 third (just behind Changemyluck) in race won by 300-1 outsider here (2m, good to soft) this month; can make his presence felt again.

runners_data.name: They Want Me
runners_data.note: Non-runner declared but prominent style would suit if participating with solid recent form

runners_data.name: The Grey Venture
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs significant improvement from modest Carlisle fourth at 66-1
runners_data.comment: Second hurdle run was much better than the first; another step forward is needed, though
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner who bettered his inauspicious rules debut when 66-1 fourth at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) this month; needs to take another good step forward here, though; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Changemyluck
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent placed form who finished ahead of Bogha Baiste last time

runners_data.name: Melbourne Ghost
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who looked unenthusiastic when fifth here last month over 2m5f
runners_data.comment: Not beaten that far when fifth here last month but needs significant improvement today
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten that far when fifth of seven here (2m5f, good to soft) last month, his second hurdle start, but looked unenthusiastic and needs significant improvement to feature today.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent style but was tailed off at 250-1 on hurdling debut at Wetherby
runners_data.comment: Tailed off when 250-1 for last month's hurdling debut at Wetherby (2m, good)
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off when 250-1 for last month's hurdling debut at Wetherby (2m, good).

races.paceDynamic: Smoke Trail, Thorneylands and Nobotheratall will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to engage early. This creates a searching test of stamina over the extended 2m2f trip, particularly as Smoke Trail has shown the ability to make all and both Thorneylands and Nobotheratall have prominent tendencies. The sustained pace will stretch the field out and expose any stamina limitations. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish through tired leaders, with prominent runners also well-placed if they can settle off the fierce early gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too hard early and tie up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop set by Smoke Trail, Thorneylands and Nobotheratall will create perfect conditions for closers to sweep past tired leaders. Hold-up performers like Herja and Bogha Baiste can exploit their stamina reserves when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Smoke Trail can dictate terms and kick clear when the pace slackens.
scenarios.body: Having made all to win his maiden, Smoke Trail uses his class edge to control the tempo and has enough left to resist challengers. His OR 118 gives him a significant ratings advantage over most of this field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Changemyluck or Hashtag Queen can sit close enough to the pace without getting involved early.
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will set up perfectly for a horse that can track the leaders without engaging in the early battle. Recent form suggests these prominent runners have the tactical speed to capitalise when the front-runners weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Steadies Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners become more tactical and the gallop steadies after the initial sparring.
scenarios.body: A slower tempo would favour the leaders who can conserve energy and potentially turn this into a sprint finish. This scenario reduces the stamina test and plays to the front-runners' tactical speed.

watchPoints.text: Smoke Trail may not handle the early pressure from Thorneylands and Nobotheratall after 51 days absence
Herja's amateur jockey Harry Sexton may struggle to time her challenge properly in a strongly-run race
The Grey Venture and Melbourne Ghost both need significant improvement and may lack the class required
Changemyluck has twice been placed behind similar quality opposition and could benefit from the strong pace
Bogha Baiste's 80-1 third last time suggests the handicapper may have underestimated his current ability

races.name: Malcolm "Scarra" Scott Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven course form but untested over this extended distance after 31 days off

runners_data.spotlight: Dual course winner (2m2f/2m5f) in the autumn; not in same form lately and untested over this far but back on a good mark and can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Jehol De Thaix
runners_data.note: Prominent tracker coming off maiden breakthrough just 20 days ago with 6lb penalty
runners_data.comment: Came good at Newcastle last month, despite some poor jumping; can improve again
runners_data.spotlight: Came good at sixth attempt, keeping on resolutely at Newcastle (2m6f, good to soft) three weeks ago; 6lb higher here but has plenty of scope for further progress if his jumping is more fluent this time.

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing hood and tongue-tie returning after 157-day absence
runners_data.comment: Absent since poor run in November and tends to save his best for Cartmel now
runners_data.spotlight: Won here in 2023 but probably better known as a Cartmel regular now (gained last two wins there); off since a poor run in November and might be of greater interest when back at Cartmel and with this outing behind him.

runners_data.name: Jericoacoara
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was close second here last month over similar distance in valuable series final
runners_data.comment: Close second in valuable series final here (2m5f) last month; must be considered
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to add to his French hurdle win in 2023 but was placed on both starts this year, more recently when close second in valuable series final here (2m5f, good to soft) last month; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Dollar Collar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing tongue-tie but fell in chase last time and showed poor effort over hurdles 18 days ago
runners_data.comment: Won this off 1lb higher in 2025 but more consistent rivals appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Now 1lb lower than when winning this race in 2025 (good ground) but fell in a chase last month and dropped out of contention rather tamely when back over hurdles here (2m5f, good; breathing issue reported) 18 days ago; might be aided by refitted tongue-tie but more consistent rivals appeal more.

runners_data.name: Starlyte
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie and pull-up headgear but 10lb claimer takes valuable weight off

runners_data.name: Magic Wave
runners_data.note: Prominent runner absent 93 days with solid course form but needs to bounce back from poor January run
runners_data.comment: Off since poor run in January but was good second over C&D just after Christmas
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner (2m5f, good) a year ago; absent since disappointing run in January but his C&D (good to soft) second just after Christmas was a good effort and he'll be right in the thick of things if back on song today.

runners_data.name: Nosy Neighbour
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces for first time with only second handicap start after good Newcastle second
runners_data.comment: Kept on for second behind Jehol De Thaix on last month's handicap debut; cheekpieces on
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who kept on for clear second behind Jehol De Thaix on last month's handicap debut at Newcastle (2m6f, good to soft); big player if first-time cheekpieces prompt any further progress.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in cheekpieces coming off good third behind Jericoacoara here 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: Back in good form lately, more notably when placed in valuable series final here (2m5f)
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form with creditable third (just behind Jericoacoara) in valuable series final here (2m5f, good to soft) last month and also ran well when second in small field at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) 16 days ago; each-way claims at least.

races.paceDynamic: Kilmore Rock will set the pace from the front with little pressure, as the only confirmed front-runner in this field. The prominent runners Menaggio, Jehol De Thaix, Secret Secret, Dollar Collar and Magic Wave will track behind but are unlikely to press the leader aggressively early. This creates a measured tempo over the extended trip, with the real race beginning from two furlongs out when the held-up horses begin their challenges. The sustainable pace and long home straight at Kelso strongly favours hold-up horses who can time their runs late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady throughout allowing closers to unleash finishing kicks
scenarios.body: The patient tactics pay dividends as Kilmore Rock sets an even gallop that plays into the hands of those held up. Heart Above, Jericoacoara, Starlyte, Nosy Neighbour and Rauzan all get the perfect setup to produce their best work late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Section Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kilmore Rock gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage while the prominent horses fail to bridge the gap effectively. Kilmore Rock's stamina proves decisive over this longer trip with the closers left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners applies pressure mid-race and sustains their effort
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and prevents the hold-up horses from getting into contention. Jehol De Thaix or Magic Wave benefit from being close enough to strike but not having to make the running throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Speed Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start with multiple horses trying to dictate late
scenarios.body: The tactical battle creates a messy race where positioning becomes crucial rather than pure finishing speed. This chaotic scenario could suit a horse like Dollar Collar who knows the track well despite recent poor form.

watchPoints.text: Kilmore Rock could set uncontestable fractions if allowed easy lead given his front-running style and recent pulled-up efforts
Nosy Neighbour faces significant step up in class from maiden company to this competitive handicap despite first-time cheekpieces
Heart Above needs monitoring over this extended 2m6½f trip having never raced beyond 2m5f previously
Secret Secret returns after 157-day layoff which raises serious fitness concerns despite course-winning form
Multiple headgear changes on Menaggio, Secret Secret, Starlyte and Nosy Neighbour suggest connections seeking improvement

runners_data.spotlight: Dual course winner over hurdles; finished alone in a match race on seasonal/chase debut in October then wasn't beaten far when last of four over C&D (good to soft) in February; eased in grade today and could still have potential over fences.

runners_data.spotlight: Made all to land good prize at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) in January and is also very well suited by this track but he's no longer the force of old and was unable to land a telling blow at Carlisle last month; others have more appealing profiles.

runners_data.name: Joecooker

runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over fences but gave very good account when third in valuable series final over C&D (good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) last month and has been dropped 1lb since; big player if new headgear continues to help.

runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with career-best performance this month, drawing clear to win by 11l over C&D (good) on chasing debut; 9lb higher in a higher-grade race today but could easily have more to offer over fences.

runners_data.name: Carrigeen Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form figures include a fall, needs to bounce back for Micky Hammond

races.paceDynamic: Old Gregorian will lead with Breizh River and Jet Legs likely to press early, creating a genuine pace over this stamina test. The prominent runners may go too fast given Breizh River's front-running tendencies and Jet Legs returning from a break, potentially setting up a collapse. With six hold-up horses including the in-form Looking Splendid and consistent Special Rate, this becomes a tactical affair where patient riders can capitalise. This pace dynamic strongly favours hold-up horses who can pick off tired leaders in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast early and fold
scenarios.body: The pace collapses as Old Gregorian, Breizh River and Jet Legs tire, allowing the patient hold-up brigade to sweep past. Looking Splendid's recent course win and Special Rate's consistency under these tactics make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Old Gregorian sets reasonable fractions and stays strong
scenarios.body: The leader maintains control while Breizh River and Jet Legs apply pressure without overdoing it early. This creates a genuine staying test where the most reliable stayers prevail regardless of style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Breakaway
scenarios.trigger: If Breizh River takes over from Old Gregorian and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The proven course specialist uses his tactical speed to dominate, especially if he replicates his Musselburgh front-running victory. The hold-up horses get too far back on the good ground to make up sufficient ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Meltdown Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If all the prominent runners collapse dramatically in the straight
scenarios.body: Every early leader stops badly, creating a messy finish where any horse with energy left can capitalize. The outsiders and unfancied hold-up horses get their chance in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Looking Splendid could be overbet given the 9lb rise and step up in class from his debut chase romp
Old Gregorian's jumping under pressure as he has limited chase experience and may not handle being headed
Breizh River's early positioning as he could either press Old Gregorian or sit closer than ideal for his style
Jet Legs and Garde Des Champs both returning from long breaks and may need the run despite their ability
The hold-up horses getting good positions early as six of them could create traffic problems turning for home

races.name: Reg And Betty Tweedie Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dare To Shout
runners_data.note: Hold-up style horse who needs a strong pace to be effective, but hasn't fired since October and faces a tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Didn't run badly when fifth here (3m2f) last month and has become well handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Not really firing on all cylinders since scrambling home by a neck on seasonal debut at Carlisle (3m, good) in October but now 6lb below that mark, and didn't run badly when last of five finishers here (3m2f, good to soft) in March; had another wind op (his third) soon after that latest outing; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Cadell
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist with three course wins, but his recent pulled-up efforts raise stamina concerns despite the blinkers switch
runners_data.comment: Made all in new blinkers over C&D in November but pulled up three times since; now visored
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in first-time blinkers over C&D (good to soft) in November, his third course win, but was pulled up on all three subsequent outings and needs switch to first-time visor to provoke another resurgence.

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent form before his 393-day absence, but fitness must be a major question mark
runners_data.comment: Won three in a row in February/March 2025 but this is his first run since
runners_data.spotlight: In excellent form in February/March 2025, winning three in a row at around 3m (good to soft/good), but has fitness to prove after 393-day absence and will need to hit the ground running to have any chance off current mark.

runners_data.name: Walk On Quest
runners_data.note: Prominent style with two course wins last season, but disappointing recent form apart from one Newcastle second
runners_data.comment: Four wins last season (two here) but largely disappointing since; has a point to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Last season's chasing four-timer included two course wins (2m1f/2m5f) but he's been disappointing since, barring a keeping-on second at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in December; pulled up in Carlisle series final won by Wolfburg last month, and moves back up in trip with questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Erne River
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs others to come back to him, wearing tongue-tie for first time since February fourth
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way at Doncaster last time but this 11yo has become inconsistent
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well for a long way when fourth at Doncaster (3m, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) in February and remains well handicapped but this steadily regressive 11yo has become inconsistent, and others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Hudson De Grugy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent form for new stable with 8-length Carlisle win last month, suits the likely pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Below form on latest outing but is 2-7 for new stable this season and enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: 2-7 for new stable since the autumn, the latter win gained by just over 8l at Carlisle (3m, good to soft) last month; below form when back at Carlisle a fortnight later but still considered.

runners_data.name: Wolfburg
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse coming off impressive 9-length win at Carlisle, now 11lb higher but could handle the rise
runners_data.comment: Won series final by 9l at Carlisle last month and is now 2-5 over fences; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Readily drew clear to win valuable series final by 9l at Carlisle (2m4f, good to soft) last month and is now 2-5 over fences; went up 11lb for that but could have untapped potential over this longer trip; respected.

races.paceDynamic: Cadell is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a sustainable gallop without pressure through the early stages. Red Happy and Walk On Quest may track him prominently, but with Hudson De Grugy also capable of pressing, the pace could quicken approaching the business end. The hold-up merchants Dare To Shout, Erne River and Wolfburg will need the leaders to come back to them over this staying trip. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can sit close to Cadell and strike when the pace lifts, as they'll avoid the traffic issues that could hamper the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Cadell sets reasonable fractions and the prominent horses can stay in touch
scenarios.body: The pace will quicken from three out as the trackers pounce, leaving the hold-up horses with too much to do. Hudson De Grugy or Walk On Quest can use their tactical position to full advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If Cadell goes too fast early or the prominent horses engage in a speed duel
scenarios.body: The leaders will come back dramatically in the closing stages, allowing the patient riders to sweep through. Wolfburg's stamina or Dare To Shout's class could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Cadell jumps well and no one pressures him through the middle stages
scenarios.body: He'll have too much left in the tank for the closers, maintaining his advantage all the way to the line. His course record and front-running style perfectly suit this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fitness Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy's 393-day layoff shows or other horses don't handle the ground
scenarios.body: The race will become a test of recent match fitness over the final half-mile. Those with regular recent racing will pull clear of the rusty returnees.

watchPoints.text: Cadell could fold quickly if his recent stamina issues resurface, despite his front-running advantage
Red Happy's 393-day absence may tell in the closing stages despite his previous excellent form
Hudson De Grugy's recent Carlisle form suggests he's perfectly tuned for this type of race shape
The hold-up horses Wolfburg and Dare To Shout need the pace to collapse to have realistic chances
Walk On Quest's course record gives him claims if he can recapture last season's form

runners_data.name: Interchangeable

runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two respectable efforts at Carlisle (2m1f/2m3f, soft) but was soundly beaten there on latest outing in February (raced too freely) and has now been unplaced all four starts for current stable; sports refitted hood and first-time tongue-tie here; others look safer.

races.paceDynamic: Gozo is the only confirmed front-runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead with minimal early pressure. The prominent runners Parisian Fashion and Gonnino will likely track within a few lengths, but neither has shown aggressive early tactics. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses (The Best Way, Ellistrin Bay, Big Love, Alvesta, Highly Recommended, Struth, Interchangeable), this sets up as a steadily-run affair where the pace will build gradually from the back of the last flight. This pace profile strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will develop when the large contingent of hold-up horses all look for racing room simultaneously in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Gozo handles the trip and jumping under pressure
scenarios.body: The confirmed front-runner gets his own way in front and proves hard to peg back when the hold-up horses make their move too late. Traffic problems behind help his cause as rivals get shuffled back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow for the leader to sustain his kick
scenarios.body: Parisian Fashion or Gonnino can position perfectly behind the leader and have enough tactical pace to strike approaching the last flight. The fresh Parisian Fashion looks most likely to benefit from this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large group of hold-up horses get badly hampered in the straight
scenarios.body: Multiple runners coming from behind creates a messy finish where positioning and racing luck becomes crucial. The Best Way's class could tell if getting a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Gozo stops quickly or makes jumping errors
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last flight where natural pace and fitness levels matter most. Fresher runners with recent form hold the edge.

watchPoints.text: Gozo's jumping under pressure - pulled up last time and needs to handle the sustained pace
Traffic problems in home straight with eight hold-up horses all needing racing room simultaneously
Parisian Fashion's fitness after 112-day break despite good fresh record and first-time visor
The Best Way's readiness returning from 422-day layoff having won impressively last time out
Early pace development - if too slow it will disadvantage Gozo's front-running tactics

races.paceDynamic: Hunters Spring will set a moderate tempo from the front with Fine Point and Glenridding tracking closely in prominent positions. The pace will be sustainable through the early stages with no obvious pace pressers to force the issue. This creates a rhythm race where the field will remain compact turning for home, leading to a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a late surge, as the modest early gallop will allow closers to get into contention from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains steady and the field stays bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows patient rides to pay dividends as closers sweep past tiring leaders in the final furlong. Horses with tactical speed from off the pace will have every chance to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Hunters Spring gets an easy lead and kicks clear approaching the last
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop preserves energy for a strong finish, while hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up. Prominent racers who can quicken from the front prove hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If Fine Point or Glenridding take the race to Hunters Spring from halfway
scenarios.body: The tempo lifts significantly through the middle stages, stringing out the field and creating gaps. This benefits horses with stamina who can sustain their effort rather than rely on pure finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Jumping Disrupts
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make jumping errors or fall at the hurdles
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical scramble with the pace disrupted by mistakes and unseated riders. Those left standing with clear rounds benefit regardless of running style, creating unexpected opportunities.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hunters Spring at the first few hurdles as any early mistake could disrupt the likely steady pace scenario
Monitor if Fine Point or Glenridding take the race to Hunters Spring earlier than expected, changing the complexion completely
Keep an eye on Miss Friday Lions' jumping technique given her recent poor round at Newcastle
Watch for any market moves on Ms Cindy Kate given the Nicky Richards yard is in good form recently
Observe if Lester Mail shows any signs of rustiness given his 64-day absence from the track

races.paceDynamic: The Back Braes is the only confirmed front-runner and will set a steady pace without pressure from this small field. With most runners having unknown or hold-up styles, the pace will be comfortable through the early stages before quickening from three out. The lack of pace pressure means The Back Braes can dictate terms, though his tendency to fade in the finish remains a concern. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to strike when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If The Back Braes gets an uncontested lead and maintains stamina
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits his rhythm and he can kick clear approaching the final fence before others get organized. His recent return to form and course knowledge give him every chance to finally break his maiden tag.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Performer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Phantoms Cave or Theoldboggroad can position prominently behind the leader
scenarios.body: Their superior form in points this year tells, with Phantoms Cave's easy 16-length win or Theoldboggroad's course experience proving decisive. The steady pace allows them to time their challenges perfectly from the back of the small field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Back Braes fades dramatically in the final half-mile as he has before
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the second-last fence, suiting those with finishing kicks held in reserve. Boley Bob's recent form or a rejuvenated Amma Lord could capitalize on the slow early pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders all underperform due to jumping errors or fitness issues
scenarios.body: High On The Hill's early season point wins or Bentley Road's return from a long break could surprise at big odds. The small field increases the chance of an upset if favorites fail to fire.

watchPoints.text: The Back Braes could fade dramatically in final half-mile as his record shows he struggles to see out his races.
Phantoms Cave and Boley Bob are lightly raced under rules and could struggle with the step up from point-to-point competition.
Several runners including Bentley Road and High On The Hill return from lengthy layoffs which could impact fitness levels.
Flying Skipper has the beating of The Back Braes on recent point form which could reverse if pace dynamics change.
Theoldboggroad's previous course form of finishing third here gives him a significant tactical advantage over newcomers.

runners_data.name: Eagle Warrior

races.paceDynamic: Dilrisk will take them along from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters in this small field, creating a sustainable gallop that won't burn off his stamina reserves. Cape Warrior and Midday Rendezvous can track him in the prominent positions, while Eagle Warrior will be held up at the back with the two debutants likely sitting mid-division. With minimal early pressure on Dilrisk, this sets up perfectly for the front-runner to control the tempo and kick clear when it matters. This tactical scenario strongly favours prominent runners and front-runners who can dictate terms without fierce early pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Dilrisk gets an uncontested lead and sustains his gallop to the finish
scenarios.body: The pace-setter controls every yard and kicks clear in the straight, while prominent trackers benefit from the honest tempo but can't close the gap. This rewards horses who can travel kindly behind the leader without needing a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Cooker
scenarios.trigger: If Cape Warrior and Midday Rendezvous apply sustained pressure to Dilrisk from halfway
scenarios.body: The sustained pressure forces a genuine gallop that finds out the front-runner's stamina, allowing the classier prominent runners to take over in the final furlong. Quality and fitness under pressure becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes very sedate and Eagle Warrior gets a strong ride from the back
scenarios.body: The crawling pace sets up perfectly for a late closer to sweep past tired leaders, with Eagle Warrior's point-to-point background giving him the finishing kick needed. The tactical switch from his usual style pays dividends.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If either Yorgunnarock or Teescomponents Gal shows unexpectedly sharp early speed
scenarios.body: One of the debutants breaks the expected pace pattern by going forward early, disrupting the rhythm and creating opportunities for outsiders with untapped ability. Breeding and stable confidence overcome inexperience.

watchPoints.text: Dilrisk getting a soft lead could prove decisive as no other natural pace-setter will pressure him early.
Cape Warrior and Midday Rendezvous both need to overcome inexperience under sustained pressure in the closing stages.
Yorgunnarock and Teescomponents Gal are complete unknowns whose market support could reveal stable confidence.
Eagle Warrior's hold-up style needs the pace to be strong enough to set up his late challenge.
The 37-day breaks for Midday Rendezvous, Dilrisk and Eagle Warrior suggest all three should be fresh and ready.
